text: Based on the classic presentation of a facial rash sparing the perioral area and the viral prodrome, I am strongly considering erythema infectiosum (Fifth disease) or roseola. While we await your images and the lab results, can you confirm if the rash has turned into pale "slapped cheeks" or if the child is currently in good spirits without significant lethargy? speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) caused by Parvovirus B19. The classic "slapped cheek" appearance (facial rash sparing the perioral area) combined with a subsequent lacy, pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities following a viral prodrome is pathognomonic for this condition. The absence of joint pain or "sandpaper" texture further supports this over Scarlet Fever or Roseola. No further testing is required at this time.
